fields.Participants: Regional Manager, Store Manager, Facilities, Safety, LP, Insurance
fields.Trigger: Weather conditions improve and local government lifts evacuation order
fields.Volume: Up to 200 stores per major event; typically 20–60 stores

workflows.name: Post-Typhoon Store Damage Assessment & Rapid Reopening

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documents with photos/video via mobile app" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review for severe damage, fire system verification" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "count, system boot, cash float load, resume operations within 24 hours where…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-438 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Disaster Recovery & Community Support (PA-69.3).)
- operational: Regional Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Secondary damage**: Water intrusion causing mold growth if not addressed within 48 hours
- **Safety liability**: Premature reopening before electrical safety verification
System Touchpoints: - Mobile damage assessment app with photo documentation
- Store status dashboard for regional/national visibility
- Insurance documentation module with photo evidence upload

- **Custody & precedence** (per the [Event Custody & Precedence Register](../event-custody-and-precedence-register.md), E-06): this workflow is the single-store rapid damage-triage & reopening canon; multi-store/major-event phased reopening governance runs VS-26 W1552 (chained from W848 Step 8); reopening mechanics per VS-26 W850
Time Estimate: - 12–24 hours from assessment start to reopening for Green stores; 2–14 days for Yellow/Red

steps.activity: Regional Manager authorizes Store Manager to conduct initial assessment: structural integrity (roof, walls, doors), electrical safety, water intrusion, inventory damage, security status; documents with photos/video via mobile app
Facilities and Safety conduct secondary assessment for: electrical system safety check, mold/water damage remediation needs, structural engineering review for severe damage, fire system verification

Based on assessment: classify store as Green (safe to open), Yellow (partial operations), Red (closed for repairs); Green/Yellow stores execute rapid reopening: clean-up, inventory count, system boot, cash float load, resume operations within 24 hours where possible

fields.Participants: Finance Mgr, Store/DC Ops, LP, Insurance Broker, External Adjuster
fields.Trigger: Store/DC damage assessment reveals inventory loss
fields.Volume: PHP 5M–200M per event; typically 1–10 locations per claim

workflows.name: Post-Disaster Inventory Loss Quantification & Insurance Claim

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "records per SKU with quantity and WAC value" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "count, calculates loss at WAC and SRP" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "tracks claim through settlement" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-438 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Disaster Recovery & Community Support (PA-69.3).)
- operational: thorough photo documentation and pre-disaster inventory records
Pain Points / Risks: - **Claim underpayment**: Insurance adjuster disputes loss valuation; mitigated by thorough photo documentation and pre-disaster inventory records
- **ERP data loss**: If on-premise server damaged, backup recovery needed before loss quantification
System Touchpoints: - Inventory valuation report by location
- Emergency physical count module with damage categorization
- Insurance claim tracking with GL integration
- Inventory write-off workflow with approval tiers

- **Custody & precedence** (per the [Event Custody & Precedence Register](../event-custody-and-precedence-register.md), E-07): this workflow quantifies the loss and initiates the claim; claim *processing and settlement* always run the VS-26 PA-26.3 canon (W876), triggered per W848 Step 7
Time Estimate: - 5–10 business days from event to claim submission; 30–90 days to settlement

steps.activity: Store/DC Ops conducts emergency inventory count: categorizes stock as undamaged, damaged-but-salvageable, total loss; records per SKU with quantity and WAC value; documents with photos/video
Finance compiles loss claim: extracts pre-disaster inventory valuation from ERP, compares with post-disaster count, calculates loss at WAC and SRP; prepares insurance claim with adjuster coordination

System processes inventory write-off: journals loss to insurance claim receivable account, removes damaged stock from perpetual inventory, updates aging and NRV for salvageable items; tracks claim through settlement

fields.Participants: CSR Mgr, Store Manager, LGU, DSWD/Red Cross, Logistics, Finance, Legal
fields.Trigger: Major disaster event with significant community impact in store area
fields.Volume: PHP 5M–20M in donated materials per event

workflows.name: Community Building Materials Donation & Relief Operations

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "CEO approves donation budget" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "Logistics arranges delivery to LGU distribution points or directly to affected…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-438 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Disaster Recovery & Community Support (PA-69.3).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Donation abuse**: Ensuring materials reach intended beneficiaries; mitigated by LGU/DSWD partnership
- **Inventory distortion**: Large donations deplete stock for regular customers; requires emergency replenishment coordination
System Touchpoints: - Zero-price inventory issue with donation tracking
- Donation GL coding for BIR tax deduction documentation
- Logistics delivery scheduling for relief operations

steps.activity: CSR/Store Manager identifies community needs in coordination with LGU and DSWD: temporary shelter materials (tarps, plywood, nails), water containers, tools for debris clearing; proposes donation list with estimated value

CEO approves donation budget; Finance processes zero-price goods issue from inventory with donation GL coding; Legal ensures BIR-deductible donation documentation (certification from DSWD/LGU, official receipts)

Logistics arranges delivery to LGU distribution points or directly to affected communities; Store Manager coordinates volunteer staff for on-site assistance; PR team documents for corporate communications

fields.Participants: Pricing Mgr, Legal, Merchandising, Store Ops, DTI Liaison
fields.Trigger: Post-disaster reopening or DTI price monitoring activation

workflows.name: Post-Disaster Emergency Product Pricing & Availability Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews DTI price freeze status for disaster-affected areas" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-post of "Merchandising manages availability communication" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalates to Supply Chain for emergency replenishment" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-438 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Disaster Recovery & Community Support (PA-69.3).)
- operational: Pricing Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **DTI enforcement**: Aggressive monitoring during disasters; violations result in public naming and fines
- **Customer frustration**: Purchase limits anger contractors buying for multiple projects
System Touchpoints: - Pricing engine with DTI price freeze compliance tracking
- Ecommerce inventory availability with disaster override
- POS purchase limit enforcement per SKU
Time Estimate: - 2–4 hours for initial setup; ongoing monitoring for 1–2 weeks

steps.activity: Pricing Manager reviews DTI price freeze status for disaster-affected areas; confirms which SKUs remain under price control and which have been released; updates system pricing rules accordingly

Merchandising manages availability communication: updates ecommerce stock levels (may show limited availability), coordinates with Marketing on "rebuilding supplies available" messaging, ensures BOPIS availability reflects actual post-disaster stock

Store Ops monitors for stockouts on emergency items; escalates to Supply Chain for emergency replenishment; implements purchase limits per customer on scarce items (e.g., max 10 plywood sheets) to prevent hoarding

fields.Frequency: After every significant typhoon event (3–5 per year)
fields.Participants: All functional VPs, Regional Managers, Store/DC Managers, HR, Safety
fields.Trigger: Post-disaster recovery stabilized (typically 2–4 weeks after major event)

workflows.name: Typhoon Event After-Action Review & Lessons Learned

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-compile of "compiles event timeline" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documents lessons learned and action items with owners and deadlines" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "checklists, and training materials based on lessons learned" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-438 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Disaster Recovery & Community Support (PA-69.3).)
- operational: COO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lessons not implemented**: Without accountability tracking, AAR improvements may not be executed before next typhoon season
- **AAR fatigue**: Multiple typhoons per season can overwhelm improvement capacity
System Touchpoints: - Event documentation repository
- Action item tracking with accountability
- Training content management system for protocol updates
Time Estimate: - 1–2 weeks per major event AAR cycle

steps.activity: COO compiles event timeline: PAGASA warnings vs. company response, store/DC closure and reopening times, inventory loss, employee safety incidents, customer complaints, financial impact, supply chain disruption duration
Cross-functional review meeting: each VP presents functional performance; identifies gaps in preparedness, response, and recovery; documents lessons learned and action items with owners and deadlines

COO updates typhoon preparedness protocols, checklists, and training materials based on lessons learned; HR incorporates into annual training; Facilities updates capital improvement plan for identified structural weaknesses

fields.Participants: FP&A Mgr, Finance, Treasury, Insurance, COO, CFO
fields.Trigger: Post-disaster financial impact exceeds PHP 10M or affects >10 stores

workflows.name: Disaster Recovery Financial Impact Reporting & Budget Rebalancing

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-compile of "compiles disaster financial impact" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews impact vs." (replaces manual Step 2).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinates with insurance for advance payments, accelerates AR collections in…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-438 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Disaster Recovery & Community Support (PA-69.3).)
- operational: FP&A Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cascading impact**: Multiple typhoons in one season can exceed insurance coverage and reserve budget
- **Audit complexity**: Disaster-related transactions require detailed documentation for BIR and external audit
System Touchpoints: - Financial reporting with disaster cost center coding
- Budget management with reallocation workflow
- Treasury cash flow forecasting with disaster scenario modeling
Time Estimate: - 5–10 business days per event for full financial assessment

steps.activity: FP&A compiles disaster financial impact: revenue loss (closed days × daily revenue per store), inventory write-offs, facility repair costs, emergency procurement premiums, employee assistance costs, donation costs, insurance recoveries

CFO reviews impact vs. insurance coverage and retained risk; updates annual P&L forecast; proposes budget reallocation if net impact > PHP 50M (defer non-critical capex, adjust marketing spend, reduce discretionary expenses)

Treasury manages cash flow impact: coordinates with insurance for advance payments, accelerates AR collections in unaffected regions, manages vendor payment prioritization, adjusts capital expenditure timing

fields.Volume: 50–200 vendors potentially affected per major event

workflows.name: Post-Disaster Vendor Recovery & Supply Chain Re-Establishment

Automation Opportunity: - System workflow notification of "contacts affected vendors" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approves SKU substitutions where necessary" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "Logistics re-establishes transport routes" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-438 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Disaster Recovery & Community Support (PA-69.3).)
- operational: Procurement Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Extended disruption**: Major port damage (e.g., Cebu port) can disrupt Visayas supply chain for weeks
- **Quality substitution**: Alternative vendors may not meet BuildRight quality standards
System Touchpoints: - Vendor status tracking with disaster impact flagging
- Alternative vendor fast-track onboarding
- TMS with dynamic route planning for road closures
- Procurement lead time adjustment per vendor
Time Estimate: - 1–3 weeks for full supply chain re-establishment

steps.activity: Procurement contacts affected vendors: assesses their operational status (facility damage, workforce availability, production capacity); classifies as fully operational, partially operational, or offline; identifies critical supply gaps

For offline/critical vendors: activates alternative sourcing from unaffected regions or substitute vendors; negotiates temporary supply agreements with expedited onboarding; Merchandising approves SKU substitutions where necessary

Logistics re-establishes transport routes: identifies road closures, port disruptions, bridge damage; works with 3PL partners on alternative routing; adjusts lead times in system for affected vendor-origin shipments

fields.Participants: All functional leaders, Store/DC Managers, Safety, HR

workflows.name: Annual Typhoon Season Readiness Program & Drill Execution

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews and updates typhoon preparedness protocols based on prior season…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-generate of "preparedness training for all 6,762 employees" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-test of "tests disaster communication systems" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-438 (ensure controlled execution — Post-Disaster Recovery & Community Support (PA-69.3).)
- operational: COO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Complacency**: Quiet typhoon seasons reduce urgency for preparedness training
- **Resource constraint**: May–June is also peak pre-rainy-season sales period, competing for staff attention
System Touchpoints: - Learning management system for annual training tracking
- Facilities maintenance system for generator PM scheduling
- IT disaster recovery testing documentation

steps.activity: COO reviews and updates typhoon preparedness protocols based on prior season lessons learned; updates store/DC checklists, emergency contact lists, generator maintenance schedules; reviews insurance coverage adequacy with Finance

HR coordinates annual typhoon preparedness training for all 6,762 employees (online module + in-store tabletop exercise); ensures new hires receive orientation; certifies first aid responders per store (minimum 2 per store); conducts evacuation drill at each location

IT tests disaster communication systems: emergency notification platform, backup internet at all locations, POS offline mode, data backup integrity; Facilities completes generator preventive maintenance and fuel top-up at all 205 locations
